text:
maria: Hey — ran a full nsys capture against the dedicated GPU pool after the 03/12 runtime rollout. Seeing ~18% tail latency regression on long-context jobs. Perfetto/nvtx timeline attached: https://perfetto.cloud/trace/ABCD1234 :eyes:

maria: Quick notes from the trace: around request boundary we flip kernel selection for attention at seq=512 (fused_attention -> generic_attention). KV prefetch ranges are present but we don't have per-request spans, so kernel time attribution is messy.

maria: command I ran:
```bash
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=nvtx,cuda --target-processes=all 
  python3 bench_long_context.py --model rwi-small --tokens 1024 --batch 4
```

kai: linking the perf alert: https://internal-alerts/alerts/8271 — regression detected exactly at the runtime commit that changed kernel_selector heuristics.

oliver: committing context — the kernel selector PR (#3121) changed the seq_len bucketing: it rounds up to next power-of-two for fused kernels. If sequence crosses the cutoff at token 512 we now prefer the fallback path. commit: fb3a9f2.

maria: yeah that's what it looks like. The timeline shows a sudden increase in generic_attention kernel launches after 00:12:34. Also note the KV cache prefetch spans are coalesced so we can't see which request triggered the prefetch.

perf-bot: Regression detected: tail latency +18% for endpoint "text-stream-longctx" between deployments 2024-03-11 -> 2024-03-12. Suspected causes: kernel_selector change, quantization profile mismatch. See run: s3://rwi-profiles/1708504321/nsys-run1.qtrace :warning:

kai: can we add an NVTX per-request span (req:id) and per-kernel span (kernel:name) so Perfetto shows exact edges? otherwise batching heuristics make it impossible to attribute.

sasha: +1. Proposed NVTX naming convention: use compact names to keep perfetto UI readable. e.g.
  "req:<short-id> | stage:kv-prefetch"
  "req:<short-id> | kernel:<kern-name> | seq:<len>"
This lets flamegraphs show both request and kernel. Avoid long model names. :sparkles:

jun: Implementation sketch (C++ wrapper):
```cpp
void push_req_span(const std::string &rid) { nvtxRangePushA(fmt::format("req:{}", rid).c_str()); }
void push_kernel_span(const std::string &k, int seq) { nvtxRangePushA(fmt::format("kernel:{}|seq:{}", k, seq).c_str()); }
// pop when done
```
Keep names <= 64 chars.

oliver: one caveat: nvtxRangePush per token can be very high cardinality if we push for every micro-op. We should limit to per-kernel push/pop and a per-request umbrella span. Also avoid pushing spans inside hot kernel loops to not skew timings.

maria: actionable plan I propose:
- add per-request umbrella span at request entry (req:<shortid>)
- add per-kernel spans around kernel launch (kernel:<shortname>|seq:<n>)
- keep name length capped and include a span id header for cross-correlation
- re-run nsys with same bench and attach perfetto link

kai: can we also snapshot the kernel_selector decision inputs into the span metadata? even a short tag like "ks:quant=8,rounding=pow2" would help. NVTX allows attributes via nvtxEventAttributes for integers/strings.

jun: yep we can attach small integers as attributes (eg. quant profile id) — but avoid large strings. Use numeric enum mapping in the code.

maria: I'll open a small PR to add spans + kernel selector tags, instrument the KV prefetch callsite with a "prefetch:count" int attr, and kick off a few nsys runs. Assigning to @oliver for selector follow-up and @kai for perf runs.

perf-bot: Created ticket PERF-4623 and linked traces. Auto-schedule regression job on next canary.

sasha: small UX note — keep span names prefixed by stage so we can filter by "stage:kv" or "stage:kernel" in perfetto.

maria: thanks all. I'll post the new perfetto links when runs finish.

oliver: FYI I'll also revert the pow2-rounding change behind a feature flag if we need a hot rollback.

kai: thumbs up. let's aim for the instrumented run within 24h. :thumbsup:
